procedural_matters: ISR 9396 was represented by Eyal Tal Tamari.
EST 5328 was represented by Oliver Tein.
Ema Raudyte (helm to LTU 111) gave evidence as witness for ISR 9396.
Jens Haun gave evidence as a witness for the International Jury.
Tal Harari attended the hearing as an interpreter of ISR 9396.
Ants Haavel attended the hearing as an interpreter of EST 5328.
facts: RS Feva race 9 the wind was 9-10kn, small waves.
EST 5328 on port and ISR 9396 on starboard were approaching the last mark before the finish.
Just outside the zone ISR 9396 gybed to port. The lateral distance between both boats was about one boat length.
Both boats on port tack entered the zone at the same time, with ISR 9396 inside overlapped.
EST 5328 rounded the mark in a distance of half a boat width. ISR 9396 luffed and touched the mark.
Immediately after there was contact between ISR 9396 starboard side and EST 5328 port side.
ISR 9396 took a one turn penalty.
conclusions: EST 5328 overlapped at the zone failed to give ISR 9396 mark-room, and broke RRS 18.2(a)(1).
EST 5328 did not avoid contact when it was reasonably possible, and broke RRS 14(a).
ISR 9396 to windward failed to keep clear of EST 5328 to leeward, and broke RRS 11.
ISR 9396, the boat sailing within the mark-room to which she was entitled to did not act to avoid contact with EST 5328, when it was reasonably possible. ISR 9396 broke RRS 14(a).
Since ISR 9396 broke RRS 11 while she was sailing within the mark-room to which she was entitled, she is exonerated under RRS 43.1(b) for this breach.
Since ISR 9396 was sailing within the mark-room to which she was entitled to and the contact did not cause damage or injury, she is exonerated under RRS 43.1(c) for breaking RRS 14(a).
